headlines.hero: 8 models tested once on seasons they never saw. 5 passed, 3 failed.
headlines.hero_deck: 2 more are reported as development-only results: 1 negative and 1 still running live as a shadow model.
headlines.scoreboard: 5 passed, 3 failed, 1 negative result, 1 not yet tested.
headlines.chart: The game model beat Elo in all 6 seasons and finished 0.0099 Brier behind the market.

models.name: Game model
models.what: Win chance for each game from Elo, opponent-adjusted efficiency (EPA, expected points added) and the starting quarterback.
models.reading: It beat Elo in all six seasons. The market is still ahead. Its calibration error missed a bar that was too tight for 1,615 games.

primary.label: Brier score, model minus Elo (lower is better)

also.text: Brier 0.2195 against Elo 0.2231 and the Vegas market 0.2096

models.name: Margin model
models.what: The full spread of possible final margins, aware that 3 and 7 are common margins.
models.reading: Its error was lower than Elo's spread, but the interval includes zero, so the edge is not proven. It still drives the site's spreads and the simulation.

primary.label: Average margin error in points, model minus Elo's spread (lower is better)

also.text: Error 10.126 points against Elo 10.185 and the market line 9.764

models.name: Playoff odds
models.what: 20,000 simulated seasons with the real NFL tiebreakers and a season-long strength shock for each team.
models.reading: Adding the strength shock improved the made-playoffs forecast, and the odds were calibrated. Live on the site.

primary.label: Made-playoffs Brier score, with strength shocks minus without (lower is better)
primary.window: regular seasons 2020 to 2025, 4 starting weeks each

also.text: The tiebreaker code reproduces all 48 actual conference seedings, 2002 to 2025

models.name: Lineup values
models.what: A value for each player from box-score stats, and the probable lineup each team will field.
models.reading: Knowing who plays added nothing measurable to the game model on development seasons, so it was never sent to the holdout.

primary.label: Brier score, best lineup model minus the game model (lower is better)
primary.window: development seasons 2012 to 2019, no holdout run

also.text: Smaller steps: +0.0002 and +0.0004; every interval includes zero

models.name: On-field player ratings
models.what: A plus-minus rating for every player, from who was on the field for each of 177,545 plays (2016 on).
models.reading: Beat team ratings, but lost to simply adding up box-score values. Public data cannot split credit among the 22 players better than that. Kept as a descriptive view.

primary.label: Play-level squared error, RAPM minus box-score values (lower is better)
primary.window: seasons 2020 to 2025, forecast one season ahead

models.name: Kalman strength model
models.what: A team-strength rating that carries its own uncertainty, combined with Elo and the quarterback term.
models.reading: It narrowly missed the bar on development seasons, so no holdout was spent on it. It is logged before kickoff next to the live model as a clean forward test.

primary.label: Brier score, Kalman candidate minus the live model (lower is better)
primary.window: development seasons 2006 to 2019, no holdout run

models.name: Play outcome model
models.what: The whole distribution of yards a play can gain, from the pre-snap situation and personnel.
models.reading: More accurate than the situation-only baseline in every season and in both data eras. Knowing the individual players adds only a small amount.

primary.label: Yards error (CRPS), model minus the situation baseline (lower is better)
primary.window: seasons 2020 to 2025, forecast one season ahead

models.name: Win-probability model
models.what: Win chance at every snap of a game, built without any betting-market input.
models.reading: More accurate than the public nflfastR model. The Vegas-based probability is still better.

primary.label: Brier score, our model minus nflfastR (lower is better)

also.text: Against the Vegas-based probability: +0.0062 [+0.0039, +0.0086] (Vegas is better)

models.name: Fourth-down tool
models.what: Go for it, kick a field goal, or punt, compared in win probability with an uncertainty band.
models.reading: The field-goal and punt parts passed. The go-for-it conversion estimate was off, so the tool failed. A corrected version is frozen for 2026.

primary.label: Go-for-it conversion calibration error (ECE) against its limit (lower is better)

also.text: Field goal make rate calibration 0.011: passed
Punts: -0.105 [-0.126, -0.086] yards of error against the by-spot baseline: passed

models.name: Early-down play calling
models.what: Run or pass, and from which personnel group, on first and second down, using causal methods.
models.reading: The recommended mix beats what teams actually did, and the placebo check came back near zero. Defenses would adapt, so treat it as a direction, not a guarantee.

primary.label: EPA per early-down play, recommended mix minus observed (higher is better)
primary.window: seasons 2020 to 2025, forecast one season ahead

also.text: Placebo check, should be about zero: +0.006 [-0.001, +0.012]

chart.whisker_note: Whiskers show the 95% interval of each row's gap to the model (paired bootstrap).

findings.title: The quarterback is most of the story.
findings.text: In the game model, nearly all of the gain over Elo comes from knowing the starting quarterback, and it depends on knowing who actually starts.

findings.title: Player-level beats team-level, but public data limits individual credit.
findings.text: Box-score credit summed over the players on the field beats team ratings when predicting the next season. On-field plus-minus does not beat box credit, and lineup effects do not move game predictions.

findings.title: Elo's edge is memory.
findings.text: Elo carries what it learned across seasons. On development seasons our features alone tie Elo overall: Elo wins in weeks 1 to 4, and our features win in weeks 10 to 18.

findings.title: Teams are still too conservative.
findings.text: The fourth-down audit estimates about 0.03 wins per team-game given up, mostly by punting (model-estimated). The early-down policy says pass more, especially from 12 personnel on 1st and 10.

findings.title: The market is still better at game prediction.
findings.text: Brier 0.2096 against our 0.2195 on 2020 to 2025. Our models are independent of the market by design, so the edge we measured over Elo and nflfastR is real.

forward_test.name: Fourth-down conversion fix (M7a-v2)
forward_test.text: The corrected fourth-down conversion engine was frozen before any 2026 game was played. It is scored once, on the 2026 season, after the 2027-02-15 data release, with no refit.
forward_test.dev_note: On development seasons its conversion calibration error was 0.019 against 0.033 for the first version, and the 4th-and-2 gap was +0.004 against +0.034.
